summary: Feed s129_double to NDR is degraded: 98.9% encrypted bytes exceeds 90% tolerance and 60.1% of frames are ERSPAN-encapsulated, both blinding payload inspection and flow parsing.

findings.root_cause: Nearly all traffic (98.86% of bytes) is TLS/encrypted with no decryption in the visibility path. The packet broker is forwarding wire-encrypted traffic directly to the NDR without a SSL visibility/decryption appliance or decrypted mirror.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection, JA3, file extraction and anomaly detection. With 99% encrypted, it sees only headers and cannot detect C2, exfiltration, or lateral movement inside encrypted sessions.

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs cleartext payload; decrypting once at the visibility layer (or feeding a decrypted copy) restores detection coverage while keeping wire encryption intact.

findings.root_cause: 60.1% of frames (1218/2027) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel encapsulation. The packet broker/SPAN source is forwarding ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic without stripping the outer header before delivery to the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR parses outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE headers instead of inner original Ethernet/IP/TCP headers, breaking flow correlation, application identification, and detection rules; adds overhead and may cause missed detections or mis-attributed flows.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes the true inner L2-L7 headers so the NDR can correctly reassemble flows and apply its detection logic.
